GAMER-ICU: Logistics & Premise
Premise:

You are an RN on a special mission to space on the Coughluous-81 space shuttle. You have been recruited to planet AtelectaPrime to defeat Captain Collapse, the commander of the deflated lung quadrant. The only way to do this is to gain knowledge, because knowledge is power! Your mission is to travel across AtelectaPrime and collect as many PEEP points as possible over the next 90 days. Every 30 days, two regions of AtelectaPrime will become available, each with new challenges.
+ a tour guide (alien?) pops up to guide you through this premise?
Time:
20 min, ~3x/week = 60 min/week to play
Estimated total time of curriculum: 240 min/month x 3 months = total curriculum ~720 min
Compliance marked by 80% of activities completed
Regions:
6 regions total
3 months (=90 days) total
= 2 regions/month, 240 min/month = 120 min/island AND 2 islands/month (240 min/month)
All activities for the open regions are available at the start of the 30-day window. Though it is recommended to do them in order, this is not required.
Regions remain open as you progress through the months if you wish to go back and re-do activities
Remuneration:
RNs get paid:
$10 to take competency (baseline) exam
$10 to take competency (end of curriculum) exam
Eligible to take exam, regardless of how much they completed
$5 to take competency (retention) exam
$15 ($5 for each 30-day window they were compliant (completed 80% activities) x3)
If RN WINS, they can make $140 (& the glory!)
GAMER-ICU: Map

Goals & Objectives
The global goal of this curriculum is to improve pediatric ICU RN competency in IMV. Specific goals and objectives are broken down by RN IMV competency domain.

1. Domain: Medical & Contextual Knowledge  
Goal: A pediatric ICU RN who is competent in invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV)…
Integrates their knowledge of cardiorespiratory and airway anatomy / physiology into the greater picture of their patient’s disease state and illness course.
Objectives: At the end of this 90-day, gamified curriculum, pediatric ICU RNs will be able to….
List the variables associated with ventilation and oxygenation with 100% accuracy on free text questions on written exam.
Describe how the following disease processes affect oxygenation and ventilation:
Asthma
Bronchiolitis
Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
Tracheobronchomalacia
as assessed by >/= 80% on a written MCQ exam.

Systematically interpret their patient’s most recent chest x-ray (using an ABCDE approach) to determine if endotracheal tube placement is appropriate and identify any other pulmonary pathophysiology, as assessed by >/= 80% on a written MCQ exam.
Interpret arterial, venous, or capillary blood gas results and identify the most appropriate management option, as assessed by >/= 80% on a written MCQ exam.

2. Domain: Autonomous Decision  Making  
Goals: A pediatric ICU RN who is competent in invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV)…
Cultivates a sense of accountability for comprehensive patient care, including their associated ventilator equipment
Forms an accurate and holistic assessment of their patient that can informs appropriate autonomous decision making
Objectives: At the end of this 90-day, gamified curriculum, pediatric ICU RNs will be able to….
Describe the level of ventilatory support a patient is receiving by comparing current ventilator settings to physiologic values for patient’s age, as assessed by >/= 80% on a written MCQ exam.

Compose an accurate, global assessment of their patient’s disease process and severity, as well as current clinical status, by synthesizing data from physical exam, the cardiopulmonary monitor, and the ventilator screen. This will be evaluated by achieving >/= 70% congruence to an assessment statement written by the attending physician.

3. Domain: Technical Skills  
Goals: A pediatric ICU RN who is competent in invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV)…
Confidently provides appropriate hands-on care for an invasively ventilated patient.
Reduces harm for invasively ventilated  patients with hands-on care
Safely navigates an unplanned extubation or tracheostomy decannulation scenario
Objectives: At the end of this 90-day, gamified curriculum, pediatric ICU RNs will be able to….
Pre-requisite knowledge: Demonstrate correct bag-mask ventilation (BVM) on a manikin, as evidenced by achieving adequate chest rise and end tidal CO2.

Pre-requisite knowledge: Demonstrate the appropriate technique for in-line suction without causing patient harm (bleeding, hypoxia), as evidenced by their ability to select the proper depth of in-line suction on a Ballard catheter station (“skills” portion of exam).
Promptly determine if their patient is still intubated through accurately listing 3 immediate things they can check at the bedside with expected values on a free text question on a written exam.
List the necessary medication and equipment to execute a safe transport off the unit with 80% accuracy using a free text question on a written exam.
Classify an extubation readiness test (ERT) as successful or unsuccessful on a written exam, as assessed by >/= 80% on a written MCQ exam.
List at least 5 potential risk factors for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), as assessed by a free text question on a written exam.

4. Domain: Executive Functioning  
Goals: A pediatric ICU RN who is competent in invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV)…
Embodies the ability to multi-task in coordinating all aspects of patient care, while prioritizing airway, breathing, and circulation (ABCs!)
Objectives: At the end of this 90-day, gamified curriculum, pediatric ICU RNs will be able to….

Correctly judge whether an artificial airway is effectively oxygenating and ventilating a patient through rapid appraisal of their vital signs, end tidal CO2 waveform, physical exam, and ventilator interface, evaluated by their accuracy in judging 3 clinical scenarios on a written exam.
Reflect on their current practice on the continuum of task-oriented work to patient- and communication-centered work, as evaluated through written reflection.

5. Domain: Interpersonal Skills 
Goals: A pediatric ICU RN who is competent in invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV)…
Promotes interprofessional collaboration through effective communication and recognition of their roles and limitations
Objectives: At the end of this 90-day, gamified curriculum, pediatric ICU RNs will be able to….
o) Value the importance of interprofessional collaboration in enhancing patient safety during ventilator management, as assessed by a written reflection on one or more patient care encounters.
Educational Strategies
Video – a video recorded by a respiratory therapist or pediatric ICU attending or fellow physician. It will be brief, between 2-10 minutes. Nurses will get credit for completion of watching the video
Methods: Lectures

Highlights: can inform medical knowledge and / or technical skills. May be repeated for those who want to re-enforce concepts, watch again as they encounter scenarios on the unit (e.g., re-watching the video about the oscillator if caring for a child on an oscillator that day)
Reading/Graphic – a brief article, graphic, or written presentation may be assigned for the learner to review
Methods: Readings, visual graphic
Highlights: medical knowledge-based domains, passive learning
Quiz – A brief, 2-5 question test. Nurse will get a certain amount of credit for each question answered correctly
Methods: online learning, formative feedback / check-in experiences for videos and readings
Highlights: medical knowledge-based domains, active learning
Types:
Multiple choice quiz
Drag & Drop
Matching
Fill in the blank w/ a word bank
Clinical case vignettes – clinical scenarios
Medical management – Nurses are presented with images or clinical vignettes and must identify problems with current management or determine correct next steps.

Communication – Participants must “phone a friend” and summarize the scenario using SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) format to an RT or provider. AI will analyze the text and award points based on SBAR use
Methods: deliberate practice with feedback, audio, visual,
Highlights: active learning, promotes interprofessional collaboration and teamwork skills

Quest – This activity requires the learner to complete a routine patient care task in real life (e.g., correctly suction an intubated patient or patient with a tracheostomy they are caring for, boost 100% FiO2 on different ventilator interfaces on the unit that day), observed by an expert (i.e., respiratory therapist or fellow/attending). This allows RNs to learn in real time, with their actual patients (within their scope of practice), and from their co-workers in other fields, with provision of formative feedback.
Methods: deliberate practice with feedback and team training roles, peer teaching, demonstration, role models, behavioral interventions, real-life and supervised clinical experiences, demonstrations
Highlights: promotes interprofessional collaboration and teamwork skills, great for development of hands-on, technical skills

Vent Lab – This activity will have a cartoon ventilator, where nurses must interact with the interface. For example, they may observe values and be asked to identify a problem, solve a problem, or boost FiO2.
Methods: role-play, artificial models
Highlights: problem solving, executive functioning (i.e., prioritizing, multi-tasking), autonomous decision making
